subject: Post-call: Streamline Finance discovery — TCO levers & budget framing
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@streamlinefin.com>, Elena Morris <elena.morris@streamlinefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (token economics & batching levers)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while the items are fresh and to confirm the next steps we discussed: 

Pain points you confirmed:
- Generation costs are the primary blocker for broader rollout (current per-user token spend spikes on long chat histories).
- Latency tolerances are strict for real-time fraud alerts (sub-400ms tail for critical routes).
- Ops overhead: your infra team prefers minimal changes to the existing request flow.

Goals you stated:
1) Keep per-conversation cost under $0.05 average for 95% of active users.
2) Maintain critical route p95 latency <= 400ms.
3) Pilot in Q3 with 500K monthly queries to validate unit economics.

TCO levers we proposed on the call:
- Model choice + quantization: opaque LLM -> 8-bit quantized open model variant to cut per-token GPU time by ~30%.
- Batching: route non-critical async requests to a batching pool with 200ms micro-batch windows (expected savings ~38% on those tokens).
- KV/prefix caching: maintain short-term KV cache for repeated user prompts (saves 15–25% tokens on conversational reuses).
- Routing fallbacks: fallback to smaller model for low-confidence, non-critical outputs to preserve latency/SLA.

Attachments: I attached a brief MAF draft and three TCO scenarios (conservative / base / aggressive). See: streamline-maf-draft.pdf, tco-scenarios.xlsx [Attachment stubs].

Concrete next steps we agreed:
- Redwood to deliver a tailored cost model (base/conservative/aggressive) by Friday 5/29. (Action: Irene)
- Streamline to share typical sequence-length histogram and a sample of recent chat traces (PII redacted) by 6/1. (Action: Samir)
- Quick 30-minute ops sync to map integration points (target week of 6/7). (Action: Marissa to coordinate)

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag. Otherwise I’ll put the cost scenarios in HubSpot and start the ops invite.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (token economics & batching levers)

Thanks Irene — that looks right and aligned to our internal notes. A couple of clarifications from my side: 

- The $0.05 target is an average we're comfortable with for the pilot; we expect 10% of users will still be heavy (> $0.20/convo) and want to monitor attribution.
- For the latency callout: the fraud alerts are <400ms end-to-end today; any fallback routing must preserve that SLA.
- We can export the sequence-length histogram and will scrub user IDs before sending — target to share by 6/1.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product
Streamline Finance

Subject: Internal: Streamline follow-up items (cost model inputs + ops sync)

Marissa / Aditya —

Short internal sync following Samir's call. Key asks from the customer and what they expect from us: 

1) Cost model deliverable (Irene) — due 5/29: three scenarios with breakouts by route (critical real-time, standard chat, async batch), assumptions for sequence length, tokenization overhead, expected batching hit rates. Please use the attached tco-scenarios.xlsx as the template.

2) Data needed from Streamline (Samir): sequence-length histogram, 1 week of anonymized traces, and a list of top 10 user flows. We should confirm the exact format we need so they can export easily.

3) Ops sync (Marissa) — target week of 6/7: attendees should include one engineer from Streamline infra, one of our runtime engineers (Aditya), and product. Agenda: integration touchpoints, fallback policy mechanics, and monitoring hooks (token breakdown per route). Keep to 30 minutes.

Operational constraints they called out to honor: minimal changes to client SDK call patterns; prefer routing decisions on the server side. Also they want to avoid real-time KV writes that require downstream persistence.

Risks / unknowns:
- Unknown real-world batching hit rate. Our conservative scenario should assume 10% effective batching until we see traces.
- Small-model fallback quality needs quick evals; recommend we run a 1K prompt A/B to measure delta before proposing fallback ops.

Aditya: can you draft two quick eval checks we can run on an A/B sample? One for latency (p95) and one for quality (top-1 response accuracy for 1k prompts). If you can sketch the eval by EOD tomorrow I’ll include it in the cost model doc.

Marissa: please propose three 30-minute slots for week of 6/7 and I’ll share with Samir.

Thanks —
Irene
